query: The Counter at Pell's Pell's daughters ask you into the back, where Old Pell is counting drops. They want to keep you on after graduation, full time, at the counter and, one day, at the drawers that nobody else may open. "Father says you count well," says the eldest. Answer by the last day. Say yes, in principle Old Pell stops counting long enough to nod at you, then starts again from one. His daughters say that's the highest praise there is. Ask about the drawers that never open "In ten years," says the eldest, "if you're still careful." You realise you'd like to still be careful in ten years.
